---
title: "Broader Community"
---

BRUG exists within a rich landscape of data science and research communities 
at UW–Madison. Whether you are looking for statistical consulting, library 
support, a student club, or a community of practice focused on machine 
learning, the groups below are worth knowing about. We think of them as 
neighbors — different doors into the same larger project of open, rigorous, 
reproducible research.

---

## Campus Services

**[SSCC — Social Science Computing Cooperative](https://www.sscc.wisc.edu)**
Statistical computing support, consulting, and training for UW–Madison 
researchers. A long-standing resource with deep expertise in R, Stata, and 
related tools.

**[Library Research Guides — R Programming Workshops](https://researchguides.library.wisc.edu/R/why)**
UW–Madison Libraries and Ebling Library offer R programming workshops for graduate students, faculty, staff, and undergraduates working with tabular research data. Content draws from the Data Carpentry R Ecology lessons.

**[Research Data Services](https://researchdata.wisc.edu)**
A free campus resource offering consultations, training, and guidance on research data management and sharing — including data citation, open access, repository selection, and compliance with funder and publisher policies.

---

## Student Clubs

**Badger BioData**
An undergraduate club focused on biological data analysis and reproducible 
research workflows. If you are an undergraduate working with biological data 
and looking for community, this is your home base.

---

## Communities of Practice

**[ML+X](https://mlplus.wisconsin.edu)**
ML+X is a community of practice at UW–Madison that connects students, researchers, and professionals who apply machine learning (ML) methods across various domains. Hosted by the Data Science Institute, the community is designed for researchers tackling specific applications—the "X"—ranging from the social sciences to ecology and medicine
